clusters.name: Criterion A Active Symptoms
items: Grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior (DSM p.113)

criteria.thresholds: ≥2/5 symptoms for ≥1 month active; continuous disturbance ≥6 months (DSM p.113-114)

epidemiology.prevalence: 0.3%-0.7% lifetime (AOS); <0.01% (<1/10,000) for COS (<13 yrs) (DSM p.116, Dulcan p.390)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: 1:1 M:F in adults; Male predominance 2:1 to 5:1 in EOS/COS (DSM p.116, Dulcan p.390)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Males 15-25 yrs; Females 20-35 yrs (DSM p.116, Dulcan p.390)
comorbidities: Autism Spectrum Disorder (DSM p.114, Dulcan p.399)
epidemiology.prognosis: Remission ~56%, Recovery ~13.5%-30% (DSM p.117); COS/EOS poorer prognosis (Dulcan p.389)

etiology.genetic: Polygenic risk (PRS), 22q11.2 microdeletion (25-30% psychosis risk), rare CNVs 1q21.1, 16p11.2 (Dulcan p.390)
etiology.neurobiology: Mesolimbic D2 hyperdopa, Mesocortical hypodopa, cortical NMDA hypofunction on GABA interneurons, gray matter loss (Dulcan p.391-392, StahlNeuro p.90, p.95, p.105)
etiology.environmental: Winter/spring birth, urbanicity, paternal age >40, pre/perinatal hypoxia, adolescent cannabis use (DSM p.118-119, Dulcan p.398, StahlNeuro p.149)

key_side_effects: Weight gain and metabolic syndrome (Olanzapine, Risperidone) (Dulcan p.821)
treatment.monitoring: BMI percentiles and Z-scores monthly for 3 mos; Fasting glucose and lipids at 3 mos; AIMS/BARS motor rating yearly (Dulcan p.828)

high_yield: DSM-5-TR Criterion A requires ≥2/5 symptoms for ≥1 month, with at least 1 being delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized speech (DSM p.113).
In children/adolescents, Criterion B manifests as failure to achieve expected developmental milestones rather than decline (DSM p.114, Dulcan p.393).
Childhood-Onset Schizophrenia (COS, <13 yrs) is rare (<0.01%), male-predominant, and associated with accelerated gray matter loss of 3-4%/year (Dulcan p.389, p.392).
Positive symptoms stem from mesolimbic D2 hyperdopaminergia; negative/cognitive symptoms stem from mesocortical hypodopaminergia and NMDA receptor hypofunction (StahlNeuro p.90, p.95, p.105).
Lurasidone must be administered with at least 350 kcal of food to ensure adequate absorption (StahlKids p.356).
TEOSS study showed equal efficacy between FGAs and SGAs in EOS, but Olanzapine and Risperidone caused significant weight gain and metabolic risk (Dulcan p.796, p.821).
Clozapine is the gold standard for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) but requires strict ANC monitoring due to agranulocytosis risk (Dulcan p.796).
Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis is a critical medical mimic in adolescents presenting with acute psychosis, seizures, and orofacial dyskinesias (Dulcan p.241, p.397).
